text: Fig. 3.1 describes the eruption of Mount Agung in 2017.
Mount Agung is an active strato-volcano in Bali, Indonesia.
In September 2017, the area around the volcano experienced 844 earthquakes, including
350 on 26 September, and about 122 500 people were evacuated from their houses.
On 21 November, an ash cloud from the summit reached 3842 metres above sea level
and later grew to 9144 metres. Early on Saturday 25 November, some airlines cancelled
flights bound for Australia and New Zealand. An orange glow was later observed around
the crater at night, suggesting that fresh magma was moving to the surface.
On 12 December a picture of the crater was taken showing a steadily growing lava dome
occupying approximately one third of the crater. The eruption later reduced to minor
